additions.note: Multimodal flagship preview for coding, reasoning, and agents, accepting text, images, and video with 1M context. Token Plan access only; no pay-as-you-go. Preview runs November 11–25 (UTC+8), after which this checkpoint will be retired.

Non-generative multimodal decision model behind the Gemini Decisions API in Google AI Studio. Scores bounded choices and rubrics across text, images, audio, video, and PDFs, returning probabilities and confidence scores rather than generated answers.
Open world model for physical intelligence. Given a starting scene and an action described in words, simulates a video of what happens next for action-conditioned planning and simulative reasoning.

QVAC open-weight 0.8B on-device agent model for API and tool use, including multi-step everyday tasks. Designed for deployment on user-controlled hardware; benchmark comparisons in the launch are Tether's own measurements.

Apache-2.0 draft model for speculative decoding with Bielik-11B-v3.1-Instruct. Requires the target model and a compatible inference server; not a standalone language model. Publisher's scheduled November 11 release is corroborated by public weights.

Qianfan video-generation model driven by character images, text, and audio, emphasizing facial micro-expressions. Uses the November 11 API-documentation date as an availability milestone; the exact first public launch date was not established.

First post-trained checkpoint of ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base: 280B total and 14B active parameters, with 1M context for coding, agents, and knowledge work. Uses November 10 UTC OpenRouter listing; Baidu's announcement is November 11. Qianfan API is available; post-trained weights are promised later, distinct from the existing Base weights.

Long-context text and reasoning model using Baidu Sparse Attention and feedback-based history compression. Uses the November 10 UTC OpenRouter listing, with 1M context and up to 128K output; also available through Qianfan.

Apache-2.0 11B multilingual model supporting 56 languages, with function calling, structured output, and a reasoning mode. Public weights corroborate the publisher's November 10 release date; separate from the DFlash companion and planned Bielik-One decision family.
